title: Fix iCloud sync: default ON for all users + make the sync toggle actually take effect
body: ## Summary App Store review (2.76/11): "Got this app on my iPhone and iPad but the two don't talk to each other." CloudKit sync was effectively dead despite the README advertising it as the core architecture. Two bugs: 1. **Sync was OFF by default.** The store only attached CloudKit when `UserDefaults.standard.bool(forKey:"useICloudSync")` was true — which is `false` when never set. A fresh install on two devices kept two independent on-device stores. 2. **Even enabling the toggle did nothing.** CloudKit options are read once when the container is built at launch, and `migrateDataToNewStore(...)` (invoked by the Settings "Enable iCloud Sync" flow) was an empty stub: `func migrateDataToNewStore(completion:) { completion(.success(())) }`. The live container was never reconfigured → sync silently never started. Plus a macOS state bug: `@AppStorage("useICloudSync") private var useICloudSync = true` showed the switch ON while the shared store read it OFF. ## What changed - **Default sync ON for everyone.** `UserDefaults.headwayICloudSyncEnabled`: an explicit choice always wins (anyone who turned sync OFF stays OFF); otherwise it defaults `true`, so existing users upgrading from the off-by-default build start syncing iPhone↔iPad automatically. - **`reloadStore(cloudKitEnabled:)`** detaches the loaded store and reloads the *same* SQLite file with/without `cloudKitContainerOptions`, so toggling sync applies to the live container without a relaunch. `migrateDataToNewStore` now calls it. No data is copied or deleted; `NSPersistentCloudKitContainer` exports existing local records to the user's private CloudKit DB. - **Data-safety fallback** (`loadLocallyAfterCloudKitFailure`): if a CloudKit-attached store fails to load, retry loading the *same* file locally (sync off for that launch) before resorting to the existing non-destructive move-aside recovery. No branch ever deletes user bytes. - The iOS toggle's "off" path is guarded by `isCloudKitEnabled` so cancelling the migration alert doesn't tear down the store (Devin Review). ## Additional hardening (post-review pass) - **Recovery no longer breaks sync or crashes.** `handlePersistentStoreError` re-added the store with `options: nil`, silently dropping `NSPersistentHistoryTracking` (which CloudKit + remote-change handling require) and calling `fatalError` on failure. Now re-adds with the normal options, reattaches CloudKit when sync was on, and surfaces a graceful error instead of crashing. - **Real sync status.** Observe `NSPersistentCloudKitContainer.eventChangedNotification` to drive `syncStatus` from actual setup/import/export events and surface CloudKit errors; `SyncStatusView` now shows syncing / error / enabled instead of a static green tick derived from the toggle bool. - **iCloud account awareness.** When sync is on, check `CKContainer.accountStatus` and show an actionable message (sign into iCloud / restricted / temporarily unavailable) rather than silently not syncing. - **Tests** for `headwayICloudSyncEnabled` defaults (on when unset, honours explicit opt-in/opt-out) and `SyncStatus`. - Removed dead `SplashScreen_old.swift` (`LegacySplashScreen`, unused). ## Data safety / Apple compliance - **No data loss:** enabling sync reuses the existing local store in place; records are exported, not moved/deleted. Caveat: a user who *manually* logged the same entries on both devices before sync gets the *union* (independently-created entries have distinct IDs and aren't auto-deduplicated) — duplication, never loss. Deliberately not auto-deduping. - **Guideline 5.1.3 (no HealthKit data in iCloud):** verified the synced model (`MigraineEvent`) stores only user-entered fields + weather/location. HealthKit reads (sleep/HRV/cycle) are computed in memory for analytics and never persisted. ## Not changed (flagging for verification) - `aps-environment` is `development` in all three `.entitlements` files while `icloud-container-environment` is `Production`. App Store builds need the **production** APNs environment for the silent pushes that drive near-real-time sync; otherwise changes appear on next launch. Left untouched to avoid breaking signing — verify the archived build's entitlement in Xcode/App Store Connect. ## Testing Not built/tested here (no Xcode on Linux). Needs an Xcode build + a two-device test on the same iCloud account: log a migraine on device A, confirm it appears on device B. CI builds all three targets and runs the iOS unit tests. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/14bfa88ec47b485e8f8b7e6794dce658 Requested by: @VSDeorchis ---
